questions.prompt: You write a custom output style to change how the agent explains things. After selecting it, the agent stops scoping its code changes and stops verifying its work. What did you miss?
options: Nothing — that is expected, and you should switch back to Default for coding
`keep-coding-instructions: true`, which keeps the built-in software-engineering instructions alongside your style
`force-for-plugin: true`, which prevents the coding instructions from being dropped
`outputStyle` set in `~/.claude/settings.json` rather than the project settings
questions.explanation: A custom style replaces Claude Code's built-in software-engineering instructions unless `keep-coding-instructions` is true. Option 0 is tempting because the symptoms look like 'this style is for writing' — but you did not intend to change the coding behaviour, and the field is the fix.

questions.prompt: You want the agent to lead every explanation with a diagram, but only in one repository. Where do you put the style file?
options: `.claude/rules/`, because it is a project instruction
questions.explanation: A project output style lives in `.claude/output-styles/` and is committed with the repo. Option 0 is tempting because it works immediately — but a user-level style applies to every project, which is more than you asked for.

questions.prompt: Your team needs a formatter to run after every file edit, no exceptions. A teammate suggests an output style that says "always run the formatter after edits." Why is that the wrong mechanism?
options: Output styles can't mention tools, only tone
A style is an instruction the agent follows, so it can be missed; a hook runs regardless of what the agent decides
Output styles only apply to the first response in a session
A style would need `keep-coding-instructions: true` to run commands
questions.explanation: Styles are guidance, not enforcement, so a guarantee needs a hook. Option 0 is tempting because styles do read like prompts — but the problem is not what they can mention; it is that they cannot guarantee an action.

questions.prompt: You create a new custom style file while a session is running, select it, and nothing changes. What is the most likely cause?
options: The style name in the frontmatter doesn't match the file name
In the terminal, style files are read at startup, so a new file needs a restart
Custom styles must be set in `settings.json` before a session starts
The style was rejected because it has no `description`
questions.explanation: The terminal reads style files when it starts, so a file created mid-session is picked up after a restart. Option 2 is tempting because settings often need a restart — but selecting an existing style mid-session does work; it is the new file that is not read.
